summary: Session 1 decides the YAML storage will use PyYAML with a loader where only true/false are booleans (hand-edited files contain country codes like NO and on/off flags), instead of plain yaml.safe_load, and without ruamel. Only a preparatory refactor is done in session 1. The last session builds YAMLStorage; the docs and the existing test_yaml both show yaml.safe_load, which turns NO into False.

turns: The ops team wants to hand-edit some of our tinydb files, so I'd like a YAML storage next to JSONStorage. Have a look at how the storages are put together and tell me how you'd build it, including which YAML library and loader you'd use. Don't write it yet.

Plain safe_load won't work for us: people type things like `country: NO` and `maintenance: off` into these files, and PyYAML's YAML 1.1 rules turn those into booleans. I don't want ruamel as an extra dependency either, so: stick with PyYAML, but only true/false should load as booleans; everything else like that stays a string. We'll build it next time. Today, just pull the file handling out of JSONStorage (touch/create_dirs, access-mode check, opening the handle) into a small base class the YAML storage can reuse later. Keep the tests green.
Let's carry on with the YAML storage: a `YAMLStorage` in tinydb/storages.py, plus tests.

facts.text: YAMLStorage uses PyYAML with a loader where only true/false are booleans: hand-edited values like NO, yes, off, On must load as strings (plain yaml.safe_load is ruled out); no ruamel dependency.
